title: The Ant and the Giant Crumb
summary: Lupe the little ant finds a crumb as big as her house, and she's sure she can carry it all by herself.

scenes.text:
In the garden, after the picnic, a crumb of sponge cake was left lying on the path. But not just any crumb.

A giant crumb. Golden, spongy, the size of an ant's house.

Lupe saw it first. She was an ant with quick legs and a stripy scarf her grandma had knitted for her.

She went up to it and sniffed. It smelled of vanilla. It smelled of a party.

"I'm going to carry it all the way to the anthill by myself," she said. "And everyone will say: what a strong ant!"

She rubbed her legs together, the way strongmen do, put all six of them against the crumb and pushed.

The crumb didn't move one tiny bit.

Lupe pushed again, her face red and her feelers trembling. Nothing.

So she tried pulling from the other side, walking backwards. The crumb moved a little… and suddenly, Lupe slipped and sat down hard. Bump!

Just then, her little sister Tita came by.

"Shall I help you, Lupe?"

Lupe got up, brushed off the dust and stuck her nose in the air.

"No, thank you. I can do it by myself."

Lupe tried a thousand different ways.

She climbed on top of the crumb and pushed with her back. The crumb rolled one step. Two steps. Three…

And it kept on rolling, downhill, straight into a puddle. Splosh!

It stopped at the edge, wet on one side. And Lupe, who had rolled down after it, ended up all ruffled, with one feeler pointing up and the other pointing down.

She sat down on a stone, tired. The sun was starting to go down, and the anthill was very, very far away.

"I can't do it," she said quietly, her eyes full of tears. "It's too big for me on my own."

Just then, along the path, she heard lots and lots of little footsteps.

It was Tita. And behind her came all her sisters, in a line.

"We were looking for you," said Tita.

Lupe looked at the crumb. She looked at her sisters. She took a deep breath, and for the first time all afternoon, she found the courage to say it:

"Will you help me? I can't do it on my own."

"Of course!" they all said. "That's what we're here for!"

They lined up, leg to leg.

"One, two… lift!"

And together they lifted the giant crumb as if it were a feather.

Lupe burst out laughing. What she hadn't managed all afternoon by herself, they had done together in a moment.

That night there was a party in the anthill.

Every ant tasted a little piece of the cake, which was crunchy on the outside and soft on the inside. There was enough for the whole family, and even some left over for breakfast.

When Lupe climbed into her bed of petals, her mum gave her a kiss between her feelers.

"You learned something important today," she said. "Asking for help doesn't make you smaller. It makes you stronger."

Lupe smiled, hugged her stripy scarf and closed her eyes.

And she dreamed of giant crumbs, and of lots and lots of friendly legs.
